title: Review: ou, oi, oy
parentNote: No new sound today, just the three teams from this week — and the useful thing about them is that all three make your mouth move while you say them. ou drops the mouth wide open and then squeezes it small: ouch, couch, sprout. oi and oy do the opposite, starting round and pulling back into a smile: oink, spoil, Floyd. So the first question is never which letters are they, it is which way does my mouth go. Once a word is in the oy pile, the rule from yesterday finishes it: oi in the middle with a sound after it, oy on the end where the word stops. The slip to expect is a word like coin coming out as cone, because a child who does not finish the slide lands on plain oh. Say it slow and stretched — ooo-eee — and let them feel the smile arrive. If they are tired, stop after the first story; the second one keeps until tomorrow.

activities.prompt: Three teams that start with an o. Find the one that drops your mouth wide open.
Now find the one that starts round and ends in a smile.
The same smile as last time, but this is the spelling that likes the end of a word.
Two sounds, and the team is right at the front. Feel your mouth drop open.
The same shape of word, and the mouth goes the other way. Round, then a smile.
There is an l after the team, so this one has to be the oi.
A name, and an odd one. oy nearly always sits on the end, but names do as they like.
The long one. Two beats, a team in the first and a bossy r in the second.
Three words that start with a c. Two of them move your mouth and one does not.
All three begin with an s. Only one of them stops at the team.
This one is hard. The same start and the same ending, and everything is in the middle.

activities.text: A mouse did creep out and did sit up on the couch, and I did shout.
Do they want to count the coins, or do they want to boil them in a pot?
I did dig in the soil and did tug out a fat sprout and a bent coin.

activities.title: The mouse in the couch
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Floyd did flop on the couch with a bag and did munch a nut.
Then a loud sound did creep out. Ouch!
A fat mouse did pop up and did land on him.
It did grab a nut and did munch it on the spot.
Then out did pop a mouse, and a mouse, and a mouse.
Floyd did count. It is not a mouse in the couch. It is ten mouse kids.
Floyd did hoist the couch out to the porch and did tip it up.
Out did drop the nuts, the dust and a big black puff.
The mouse did not want to shift. It did just munch and munch.
Floyd did grin. The couch is for them, and the mat is for him.

questions.prompt: Floyd did flop on the couch and did munch ...
Floyd did count, and in the couch sat ...
In the end Floyd did sit on ...

activities.title: Joy and the coin tin
activities.prompt: A second story, and this one is all the slide that ends in a smile.
lines: Joy did dig in the topsoil out at the back, just past the shed.
I did tell her it is a ploy, and that a coin tin is not in it.
Her stick did hit a rock with a loud clunk.
Out did pop a damp tin, red with rust and shut up fast.
Joy did hoist it up and did bash the lid off on the step.
In it sat a coil, a bent nail and ten damp coins.
Joy did count them out on the mat. It is ten, and not a spot on them.
Then a mouse did run out, and Joy did drop the lot.
The coins did land in the soil, and the mouse did run for the shed.
Joy did grin. It is not a ploy, and it is not a tin. It is a dig.

questions.prompt: Joy did dig in the topsoil for ...
In the tin sat a coil and a bent nail and ...
Joy did drop the lot, and the coins did land ...

activities.label: The teams that do not slide
activities.prompt: ow, ea, ai, oa and ay. Say each one, and check that your mouth sits still.
